name: OrderFloor – Minimum Order & Quantity Limits for WooCommerce
author: Plugins.shop

sections.description:
Set purchasing rules without custom code. Edit six shopper notices, explain needed changes and preview carts before saving.

Free works locally without an account, payment, licence or external connection. Features never expire. Optional sharing/email choices start unchecked.

Examples you can set up in Free

  • Require a €50 order: €35 in qualifying products needs €15 more. The notice explains the difference.
  • Require three units: count eligible quantities across the cart, including repeated products.
  • Sell a product in packs of six: allow 6, 12, 18 and so on.
  • Exclude samples: bypass restrictions and exclude them from counted subtotals and units.

Uses your currency; rules can apply together.

Order limits and product quantities

  • Minimum/maximum cart subtotal before or after coupons.
  • Minimum/maximum total units per order.
  • Product/variation quantity limits, pack multiples and starting quantities.
  • Store defaults and variation inheritance: blank inherits; zero disables. Free checks each variation separately.
  • Stock-aware Classic/Blocks controls, including shared variation stock and held reservations.
  • Optional Classic pack dropdowns; native Blocks controls.
  • Server-side Classic/Blocks cart and checkout validation.

Clear guidance for shoppers

Default notices explain qualifying amounts/units, corrections, coupons and exclusions. Supported product forms explain when stock cannot satisfy a pack.

Edit six notices: minimum/maximum spend and units, pack multiples and whole units. Use plain-text wording and value placeholders.

Try a rule before applying it

Spend, quantity and pack presets show passing/blocked examples and change your draft only. Test catalogue products in Cart preview, review the comparison and save.

Try the Free interactive demo | Read the guides | Get support

Video tutorials: spend, quantity and packs

Watch the walkthrough for the rule you want to set, then follow its written guide.

1. WooCommerce Minimum Order Amount: Free Plugin Tutorial

Set a minimum cart amount and check what shoppers see below the limit.

Read the minimum order amount guide

2. WooCommerce Minimum Order Quantity: OrderFloor Free Plugin Tutorial

Set a minimum number of eligible units across the cart and test passing and blocked quantities.

Read the minimum order quantity guide

3. WooCommerce Sell in Packs

Set pack multiples such as 6, 12 and 18, then check valid and invalid quantities.

Read the sell-in-packs guide

Optional OrderFloor Pro add-on

Pro adds rules for existing wholesale/customer roles, product spending limits, category requirements, mixed cases of one parent’s variations and visual progress. Tools include CSV, reviewed bulk edits, mapped transfers, resumable jobs, named test suites, schedules and handover reports.

Pro is a separate paid plugin. Its editing/tools require initial online licence activation; WordPress Multisite activation is not supported. Explore Pro shows local examples. The Pro previews switch hides optional suggestions for your account on this site; Explore Pro remains available. Previously dismissed suggestions stay dismissed when previews are turned back on.

Compare Free and Pro

Requirements and supported scope

Requires WooCommerce 8.3+, WordPress 6.5+ and 64-bit PHP 7.4+. Supports Classic/Blocks cart and checkout and HPOS. Product fields use WooCommerce’s classic Inventory and Variations editors, not the block product editor.

Set quantity rules on simple products or use variable-parent defaults with variation overrides. For grouped products, edit each child product; grouped-parent rules are not inherited by children. External products do not use your store’s checkout, so they have no local quantity-rule controls.

Uses whole units. Fractional quantities, bundles/composites, subscription renewals, third-party quick-order flows and currency-conversion plugins are unsupported. Orders created directly in admin or through the orders REST API, and existing-order payment pages, are outside enforcement. Complex or split-line carts may fall back to ordinary controls and server validation.

Subtotal excludes tax, shipping and fees. Currency changes do not convert saved limits. The tester does not apply coupon codes or simulate stock, shipping, payments or every extension. Test passing and blocked storefront carts with your theme and checkout extensions before going live.

While rules are enabled, a qualifying product line with a negative amount blocks checkout with a notice; it cannot offset a maximum. This applies to the selected before/after-coupon basis. Excluded products and negative fees do not count toward these rules. Paused rules remain paused.

If saved configuration cannot be read, checkout stays blocked and the settings page explains recovery. The plugin does not replace the damaged configuration with defaults. On a 32-bit PHP host, checkout is also blocked until the host switches to a 64-bit PHP runtime.

More from Plugins.shop

OrderFloor is part of the Plugins.shop collection. Explore optional tools for other jobs around your store and website; none is required to use OrderFloor.

Useful alongside OrderFloor

  • OrderWorth — Review order contribution after recorded costs, expenses and refunds to inform minimum-order decisions.
  • StockControls — Track stock changes, receive purchase orders and plan replenishment alongside quantity and pack rules.
  • Frictions — Investigate WooCommerce checkout errors with privacy-conscious session replay.
  • WishlistGenius — Let shoppers save products, add private notes and share wishlists.

More tools for your store and website

  • Cartdini — Checkout questions and saved order answers.
  • CatalogFAQ — Reusable answers for pages and products.
  • CampaignBars — Announcements, countdowns and copyable coupons.
  • ClickClue — Visitor session replay for WordPress.
  • KillerConversions — Enquiry forms and entry management.
  • CustomFields.com — Reusable fields, repeaters and content displays.
  • Logged.ai — WordPress site activity and change history.
  • Shieldlume Security by Antivirus.ai — Local malware scanning and file-integrity checks.

Privacy and external service

Rules run locally; no shopper profiling or customer/order data is sent. Local storage: settings, ten revisions with editor ID/time (no timed expiry), and one-hour recovery drafts. Browser preferences remain until cleared. Support reports contain versions, plugin names and redacted rules; review them before sharing. They are not sent automatically.

Optional welcome service: two independent unchecked choices. Skip, close or save neither to send no welcome request. Updates do not broaden earlier permissions.

  • Compatibility sharing sends the site domain, WordPress/PHP versions and site language.
  • Email signup sends your editable email and Free/Pro edition; confirmation is required. New subscriptions start with tips, releases, weekly blog articles, offers and all current interests selected. Email preferences control topics, frequency and unsubscribe; existing choices stay unchanged. Purchase-history personalization and link tracking start off. Offers require consent and a recent Free report.

Selected data goes by verified HTTPS to https://orderfloor.com/newsletter-api/v1/plugin-welcome/ with a random connection ID, protected credential and consent version. The service receives the network address and stores credential hashes and consent/report times. Email-only signup sends no site domain. No customer data, orders, names, rules or plugin lists are included.

Reports refresh weekly, with edition-change reports/retries as needed; WP-Cron depends on traffic. Manage welcome choices to stop either scope or retry failed removal. Site-address changes pause reporting. Stopping email sharing cancels pending signup and removes the edition report; confirmed subscriptions require the email unsubscribe link. Uninstall removes local credentials without contacting the service.

Retention: inactive report/control data 90 days; pending signup 48 hours; confirmed subscriptions at most 730 days; consent/suppression 180 days. Cleanup/backups can delay deletion. WordPress privacy tools cover local email choices; a keyed retry fingerprint remains until remote removal succeeds.

Previous installation sharing: older consented connections send daily HTTPS reports to https://orderfloor.com/installation-api/v1/: hostname, random installation ID, edition/plugin versions and consent version for statistics/support. Stop/delete them in Previous installation sharing. Records expire after 90 inactive days; deletion retries last up to 90 days. A pseudonymous revocation fingerprint has no expiry to prevent recreation. No email, customer, order, visitor or settings data is reported.

Privacy policy and retention details | Pro purchase terms

The Pro previews choice, individual suggestion dismissals and chosen setup goal are stored locally for each WordPress user on this site until changed or removed on uninstall. They are not sent to Plugins.shop or OrderFloor. More Plugins uses bundled descriptions and logos; product websites open only when you follow their links.

Readable source included; no build step or external asset CDN.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce 8.3 or later.
  2. Go to Plugins > Add New Plugin, search for OrderFloor, then install and activate. Alternatively, use Upload Plugin with the individual Free ZIP.
  3. Open WooCommerce > OrderFloor. Choose an example or enter limits.
  4. Try Cart preview, choose Review changes and confirm the save.
  5. For product quantities, use Products > Edit > Inventory > OrderFloor quantity rules; use Variations for overrides.
  6. Test your storefront, including relevant coupons and variations.

Blank or 0 disables a storewide limit; product/variation rules can still apply. Back up before updating and replace without uninstalling. For this release, update Free to 1.13.14 and keep the separate Pro 1.13.13 add-on; no Pro replacement is required.

Free uses standard WordPress plugin updates. You can also upload the latest Free ZIP and choose Replace current with uploaded. See Tools & testing > Support & updates.
sections.faq:
Can I set a minimum for one product?

Free sets product/variation quantities and packs. A product-specific monetary minimum requires Pro; Free spending limits cover the qualifying cart.

Does a minimum of five and a pack size of six allow 5, 11 and 17?

No. Valid multiples are 6, 12, 18 and so on. The minimum sets the floor, not the sequence origin.

Can I keep my own shopper messages?

Yes. Store rules > Messages supports {label}, {target}, {current} and {remaining}. Blank uses standard wording; custom messages keep their wording on update. Remaining-amount notices are Free; visual progress is Pro.

Is there a setup wizard or required signup?

No. New installations open Store rules after ordinary manual activation. Optional welcome choices may appear after saving an active limit. Review these choices from the footer at any time.

Can I hide Pro previews?

Yes. Use the On/Off switch in the Free sidebar. The choice is saved for your WordPress account on this site and applies to optional sidebar previews and contextual suggestions. It does not reset individual dismissals or change saved rules, sharing choices or licences. Explore Pro and More Plugins remain available.

Does More Plugins install anything or track me?

No. Its descriptions and official logos are bundled with OrderFloor. Following a product link opens that product’s page in a new tab; the collection does not install plugins or enrol you in marketing. Each plugin has its own requirements and availability.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivation keeps settings and stops reports. Deletion removes Free’s local welcome choices, credentials and temporary forms. Enable Delete data on uninstall to remove its settings, revisions and product-rule fields too. Pro has a separate deletion preference. Products/orders remain. Cached drafts expire within an hour; clear browser copies, exports and backups separately. Disconnect sharing before deletion to request remote removal; unsubscribe confirmed email subscriptions through their email link.
sections.changelog:
1.13.14

  • Limit editable product quantity rules to simple products and variable-parent defaults; explain grouped-child rules and external checkout.
  • Preserve existing unsupported-product metadata without allowing it to block store-default changes.
  • Block negative qualifying line amounts with a clear notice instead of letting them offset order maximums.
  • Keep checkout blocked with an actionable settings recovery page when saved configuration cannot be read, without overwriting it.
  • Complete independent deactivation cleanup even if optional sharing state cannot be paused; preserve malformed records and log failures.
  • Require 64-bit PHP to prevent unsupported integer-range comparisons. Existing 32-bit sites show recovery guidance and cannot silently pass orders.

1.13.13

  • Add a persistent Pro previews switch while preserving existing dismissed suggestions.
  • Refine the sidebar, publisher attribution, documentation and support links.
  • Add all 16 companion plugins with bundled official logos and individual product links.
  • Improve installation guidance and show Free features and the demo before tutorials.
  • Saved rules, checkout enforcement and sharing choices are unchanged.

1.13.12

  • Clarify Free features, setup, update instructions and the optional Pro add-on.
  • Improve the plugin name and directory description for WooCommerce store owners.

Older notes: changelog.txt or release history.
